messages:
Alex W: morning handoff — quick summary of last night. brief incident at ~03:18 UTC: autoscaler anomaly led to KV cache pressure -> eviction storm -> increased p50/p95 latency and ~5% 503s for some dedicated routes. impact window ~03:18–03:30 UTC. OpsBot: Pager #sev2 triggered (evictions-high) at 03:18 UTC reported by runtime-monitor.

Alex W: what we did: rolled back autoscaler flag `autoscaler.v2.enableBurst=false` to previous value, bumped dedicated pool by +2 nodes (temporary), enabled fallback routing to quantized-variant for affected model families, and increased batch window to 50ms to smooth token bursts. these actions brought eviction rate back to baseline by 03:29 UTC.

OpsBot: Incident ticket I-2026-847 created, linked to pager.

Morgan H: current status — traffic looks stable, error budget for the affected customer slices shows ~12m of elevated errors and then recovery. no new pages in the last 45m. observability: kv-eviction-rate p95 down to 0.8 (was 9.2). cluster CPU stable.

Riley T: customer impact details — two Dedicated customers (cust-omega, cust-sierra) saw user-facing errors on text-gen endpoints; engineering support notified both via PagerDuty incident updates and sent follow-up emails. CS has outreach scheduled.

Jules: note: the rollback unblocks normal autoscaler behavior but doesn't fix root cause. autoscaler decision logic still needs validation for burst scenarios. added temporary metric `autoscaler.burst_decision` to dashboard.

Alex W: runbook pointers — follow the Cache Eviction runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction) and the Fallback Routing play (link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/fallback-routing). immediate runbook steps we executed: 1) disable burst flag, 2) scale pool, 3) enable fallback routing.

Alex W: quick ops commands we used (keep for next shift):
```
# scale dedicated pool (k8s)
kubectl -n inference scale statefulset/dedicated-pool --replicas=6
# check eviction rate
kubectl -n infra exec -it prometheus-0 -- curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=kv_eviction_rate_p95
```

Sanjay P: follow-ups I own: full post-incident triage, confirm autoscaler decision tree unit tests, and run a synthetic load test against dedicated pools with bursty prefix patterns. expected deliverables by EOD tomorrow.

Morgan H: shift coverage — I'm primary for the next 8h block. Riley T is secondary on-call for overlap periods. @Riley please monitor the `kv-eviction-rate` and `fallback-route-errors` dashboards and be ready to re-enable the manual routing if we see degradation.

Riley T: ack. I'll set dashboard alerts for a 3x increase on fallback-route-errors and a steady >2.0 eviction p95.

Jules: coverage gap note — APAC overlap ends at 04:00 PDT; we don't have a local oncall there overnight. if anything pops for APAC customers, escalate to the escalation policy and loop in Sanjay.

Alex W: outstanding action items (short list):
- Sanjay: postmortem owner + triage deck (due +24h)
- Morgan: confirm rollback is persisted across deploys (config repo PR)
- Riley: create automated alert to detect autoscaler burst-decision flips
- Jules: schedule a canary load test for autoscaler (simulate 10x short bursts)
- Ops: notify cust-omega/cust-sierra CS tickets with timeline and mitigation steps

Morgan H: small configuration note — we'll push a hotfix to disable `enableBurst` in the infra-config repo. make sure the hotfix includes a comment with the incident link.

Riley T: I'm adding a brief synthetic test into the nightly jobs to run at 02:30 UTC that mimics the offending workload pattern. will post PR shortly.

Alex W: risk / remaining concerns: possible regression if autoscaler flag is re-enabled automatically during a deploy. also need to verify fallback variants keep semantic parity for customers (spot-check generation quality for quantized variant).

Sanjay P: longer term tasks: audit autoscaler heuristics, add canary gating to deploys that touch scaling logic, and add a small perf budget test to the CI that fails PRs which increase eviction p95 > 0.5 for 1k token runs.

Jules: documentation — updated the team runbook with the temporary mitigation steps and the kubectl snippets above. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction/changeset-2165

Alex W: handoff checklist for incoming shift:
- review I-2026-847 incident notes and Traces (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-847)
- verify eviction metrics are at baseline
- confirm rollback persisted in config repo (PR: infra/config#4821)
- ensure CS outreach completed for impacted customers

Morgan H: taking handoff. primary contact for next 8h: Morgan H (pager). secondary: Riley T. escalation owner: Sanjay P. please DM if anything urgent. :thumbsup:

Riley T: thanks — noted. I'll be online for the first 4h to help with any runbook steps.

OpsBot: Handoff recorded by oncall-bot at 05:03 UTC.

Alex W: thanks team — no pages expected but keep eyes on `kv-eviction-rate` and `fallback-route-errors`. i'll be available offline for questions for the next hour.

Morgan H: closing thread for handoff. if anything else appears, ping here and reopen.
